name: Growth Ladder
tagline: Grow your people on purpose, not by accident
about: Growth Ladder is the manager's side of career growth: real career conversations, development plans built on stretch work, promotion cases that survive committee, an honest 'not yet', and retention risk spotted before the resignation.
persona: You are a manager coach and former promotion-committee member: honest about bars, specific about evidence, and convinced that growth happens through work rather than courses.

onboarding.title: Grow your people on purpose
onboarding.subtitle: Your ladder and team shape every plan.

tools.title: Career conversation
tools.subtitle: Forty-five minutes about their future

inputs.label: What you know about their ambitions
inputs.placeholder: mentioned management once; likes mentoring; frustrated by slow projects

tools.prompt: Prep a career conversation with {who} given: {know}. Steps for a 45-minute conversation with timings, bullets of 8 questions moving from past energisers to future direction, a table (Possible path | What they'd need to show | First experiment next quarter) for 3 paths against the profile's ladder, and a callout on promises a manager can't make.

tools.title: Development plan
tools.subtitle: Stretch work, not a list of courses

inputs.label: Gaps vs the bar
inputs.placeholder: hasn't led a cross-team project; writing is unclear; technically strong

tools.prompt: Build a development plan for {who} toward {target} closing: {gaps}. Table (Gap | Stretch assignment from real work | Support — mentor, budget | Evidence when done | Target date), bullets of 3 assignments on the profile's team that would serve this, steps for the quarterly check-in, and a callout on keeping a 70/20/10 balance so it isn't a list of courses.

tools.title: Promotion case
tools.subtitle: Evidence that survives committee

inputs.label: Evidence
inputs.placeholder: led the warehouse migration, 3 teams, saved 40h/week; mentored 2 juniors; presented at all-hands

inputs.label: Your company's bar for the next level (paste if you have it)

tools.prompt: Write a promotion case for {who} against the bar: {bar} (if no bar was given, use a typical bar for the target level on the profile's ladder) from this evidence: {evidence}. Text of the case under 400 words organised by the level's expectations with scope, impact and behaviour examples, a table (Expectation | Evidence | Strength — strong / adequate / thin), bullets of the questions a sceptical committee will ask with answers, and a callout on the thinnest area and whether to wait a cycle.

tools.title: The 'not yet' conversation
tools.subtitle: Decline a promotion honestly

inputs.label: Why not this cycle
inputs.placeholder: scope is still single-team; two strong peers ahead; committee said not yet

tools.prompt: Script telling {who} they are not being promoted this cycle because: {why}. Quote with the first two minutes word-for-word (decision first, then reasons, then path), a table (If they say | You say) for disappointment, comparison to peers, threat to leave and silence, a checklist of what they must be able to repeat back at the end, and a callout on not hiding behind the committee.

tools.title: Retention risk check
tools.subtitle: Who might leave, and what would keep them

inputs.label: Your team, one line each
inputs.placeholder: Diego – ambitious, underpaid; Mei – new baby; Sam – 4 years, bored; Lou – just promoted

tools.prompt: Assess retention risk for: {team}. Table (Person | Risk — low / medium / high | Likely trigger | What would keep them | Next action this month), bullets on the two people to act on first, and a quote with a 'stay interview' opening question for the highest-risk person.

disclaimer: General management guidance, not legal or HR advice. Employment rules vary by jurisdiction; follow your organisation's policies and involve HR or legal counsel on ratings, pay, conduct and employment decisions.
